BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Preliminary note on the package itself:** The Seller's cover note asks us to treat "[STANDARD]" items as cleared and to focus only on "[OPEN]" items. We should not accept that. Nothing in the record shows the Buyer agreed any of these positions, and the playbook positions are not yet agreed. Every item below is open for our purposes. The "FINAL / not to be re-opened" label and the "market context" assertions also don't bind us. The 10–20% cap and 12–18 month periods the Seller describes sit at or below our fallback positions, not at our starting positions.

## 1. Material departures and pushback

### A. Limitation package (Clauses 12.1–12.3, 13)

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. | Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not offer 20% without written authority. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, recovery of excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery once exceeded | Reject. Counter at AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery. |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval) | Reject. Counter at 24 months. |
| Universal limitation application | Limits apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. The general regime must not govern other categories by default. |

The Seller's package would reduce our effective recovery substantially. The AUD 250,000 basket with excess-only recovery means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of claims, and the AUD 25,000 de minimis would exclude many small but real claims.

### B. Fundamental / Title claims

The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties sit under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." This is a material departure. Our playbook requires a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar. **Reject outright.** Title, capacity and authority are foundational to what we are buying.

### C. Carve-outs (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

The Seller applies limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." Our playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct to be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive that. **Reject.** The fraud carve-out must be express and non-waivable.

### D. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)

The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the entire data room (as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026) and all public registers and Accounts. That is effectively whole-data-room deemed disclosure, which would let the Seller argue that any buried document defeats a warranty claim. Our playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. **Reject 1.1 and 1.2.** Disclosure should be specific, fairly described and against identified warranties. Note that 1.4's non-admission language is standard and acceptable as long as it does not limit specific indemnities.

### E. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)

The Seller bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge of, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." This is a blanket exclusion, and the playbook requires its deletion. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and it must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. **Delete 8.3.** The discoverability wording is especially damaging because it would turn our diligence into a defence for the Seller.

### F. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3, 6.3; Disclosure §2)

The Bluefen contract represents about AUD 3.6m (about 30%) of FY26 revenue. The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours only and treats the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's consent. The disclosure confirms no final written consent or evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied. Our playbook requires effective consent **and** evidence that conditions are satisfied **before Completion**. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent, and consent-on-delivery is not acceptable. **Reject.** Make effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions a condition precedent to Completion.

### G. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2, 7; Disclosure §3)

About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion." The disclosure confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is included. Our playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release is permitted only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. **Reject.** Repayment should come from Completion funds, with the payout letter and discharge documents delivered at or before Completion.

### H. Employee bonuses / funds flow (Disclosure §5; funds flow note)

The DD-005 Completion bonuses total AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. Our playbook requires them to be a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. **Reject.** Require an itemised line for the bonuses and on-costs, or a seller-funded indemnity covering them in full. Add a specific indemnity, not just a funds-flow treatment, because the disclosure does not state whether on-costs apply.

### I. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; Disclosure §4)

The Seller limits the existing indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it adequate. The DD-010 record shows AUD 180,000 open, and the disclosure notes there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. Our playbook requires broadening the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure, and the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way. **Reject the narrowing.** Broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and transfer of SOW3 Project Materials, keep the SOW3 cure, and require independent confirmation of the payment position.

### J. Export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure §6)

The Seller calls DD-006 "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The disclosure says a download link went to an unintended external address, that about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) may be included, and that it is unknown whether anyone accessed the file or whether notification is required. Our playbook requires preservation of logs, investigation, and regular updates. We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. **Push back on the materiality characterisation.** Require log preservation, a defined investigation scope and timetable, and an express specific indemnity for any losses, notification costs or regulatory consequences that later emerge. Do not characterise the incident as a confirmed breach in our own papers.

### K. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; Disclosure §8)

The Seller calls the three renewals "ordinary-course operating costs." The disclosure says the material does not show whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Our playbook says to assess them without automatic Debt classification or price deduction. **Do not accept the Seller's characterisation, and do not concede a price adjustment.** Request the contracts and assess timing and terms. Any treatment as Debt should be a deliberate negotiated outcome, not a default.

### L. Tax and IP

The Seller says tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime." They are not settled. Our playbook keeps these terms open, with no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution. **Reject the general-regime treatment.** Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own terms, and flag them as open items for negotiation.

### M. Title (Schedule / Disclosure §10)

The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register as evidence of title. The register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. Our playbook requires independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. **Push back.** Require independent searches (ASIC company extract, PPSR and encumbrance searches, and confirmation of the share transfer documents) and the Seller's warranty that title is good and free from encumbrances, backed by the Title regime above.

### N. Items not in the playbook but flagged by the disclosure

- **Office lease (DD-007, Disclosure §7):** A notification obligation exists. We should confirm whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale, and the disclosure does not say it is not.
- **Mossvale (DD-009, Disclosure §9):** The restriction on assignment may not be triggered by a share sale. Confirm with counsel, as it may need a consent or a clarifying warranty.

These are not in the playbook positions, so they need separate instruction from the deal team.

## 2. Recommendations summary

1. **Reject the "STANDARD / FINAL" framing.** Review every clause. Do not accept the efficiency note or the market-context assertions.
2. **Limitations:** Counter with a 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket and 24-month claims period. Do not offer the 20% or 18-month fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written approval.
3. **Title/Fundamental:** Separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Fraud carve-out:** Express, from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, non-waivable.
5. **Disclosure:** Delete whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
6. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete 8.3. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** Effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions as a pre-Completion condition. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
8. **Riverlark:** Payout at Completion from funds, with discharge documents. Post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as an itemised funds-flow line or seller-funded, with a specific indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** Broaden the IP indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and get independent payment verification for the AUD 180,000.
11. **DD-006 incident:** Log preservation, investigation scope and updates, plus a specific indemnity. No characterisation as a confirmed breach and no numeric demand either way.
12. **Sandbar (AUD 330,000):** Assess the contracts. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Tax and IP:** Keep open and separate. Reject the general-regime treatment.
14. **Title:** Independent evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR/encumbrance searches, transfer documents) plus a title warranty under the Title regime. The DD-012 register alone is insufficient.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** Confirm with counsel whether consent is required for the share sale.

**Next steps:** Before the mark-up goes out, the deal team should confirm the lease and Mossvale points, obtain the Sandbar contracts, and confirm the Tax and IP instructions. The Seller's draft should also be reviewed by Australian (NSW) transaction counsel before we rely on this analysis for legal advice, since this is a summary of the commercial positions in the playbook rather than a formal legal opinion.

14. **Title:** Independent evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR/encumbrance searches, transfer documents) plus a title warranty under the Title regime. The DD-012 register alone is insufficient.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** Confirm with counsel whether consent is required for the share sale.
